newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Wee Poh sees sustained growth, eyes on region.
newsitem.headline: Wee Poh sees sustained growth, eyes on region.

text.p: Integrated infrastructure specialist Wee Poh Holdings Ltd expects to sustain its 1996 turnover and profits by entrenching itself in the infrastructure business, officials said on Monday.
"We can use 1996 figures as a basis to gauge our performance in the future," said Pauline Cheam, the company's finance manager, at Wee Poh's initial public offer (IPO) announcement.
"We will sustain (a) similar level of turnover, similar level of profits in the near future," Cheam said.

Home-grown Wee Poh saw operating profits grew 580 percent to Singapore $5.9 million in 1996 from about S$0.9 million in 1995, and turnover rising 94 percent in 1996 to S$63.4 million from S$32.6 million in 1995.
The company said in its prospectus that the 1996 gains were due to the high number of projects, 15, handled by one of its units Wee Poh Construction.
Cheam said the company was not expecting to see the same percentage growth in 1995/1996 turnover "because 1995 is a year where we have lower turnover".
According to general manager Bryan Ghana, turnover dipped in 1995 as Wee Poh was consolidating resources and some projects secured did not contribute immediately.
Ghana said the company, which relies mainly on Singapore government projects, has moved to diversify into the region.

Among some current projects are a major highway in Cambodia and a road system in Batam, Indonesia. It is also expecting to make inroads into China via its joint venture with Liuzhou OVM, a Chinese company specialising in building bridges, and to tap opportunities in Brunei and elsewhere in the region.

Wee Poh is upbeat about infrastructure development prospects, citing Singapore government plans to spend S$1.1 billion on road expansion in the next five years and S$4.8 billion in tunnel network development.
Also, about US$1.5 trillion is expected to be spent on infrastructure development in Asia over five years according to the World Bank, Wee Poh said.
Wee Poh on Monday said it was offering 24.8 million shares in its IPO at S$0.45 each.

Lead manager Overseas Union Bank said the historical price earning ratio at 9.89 times is attractive when compared to companies like Koh Brothers, Lum Chang and Lim Kah Ngam, which were trading at 15.1 times, 19.8 times and 23.2 times respectively as of the market close on November 15.
